title: The Radio Questions and Concerns Show
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0949.txt, subs_resolved/0950.txt (729 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention. case_type: murder. The old low-fidelity case file had the correct culprit (Yashiro Kaede) but was drastically under-built: it reduced a multi-layer frame-up conspiracy to two flat 'events' and a single clue. Corrections made against the transcript: (1) the killing did not happen after 'calling the victim outside' -- Yashiro went to Towako's apartment late at night and Towako answered her own door ('What do you want? It's the middle of the night.'); (2) the old file omitted the entire mechanism of the frame-up: Yashiro forged a fake listener letter (fronted by her friend Morikawa Tsugumi under the initials 'TM', matching victim Manda Towako's initials) to bait upstairs neighbor Kijima Kumi into a public radio-show grudge and a real-life confrontation with Towako, then separately husband Teruomi Manda (unaware of the murder plan) copied the broadcast onto a CD and planted it in Kijima's mailbox hoping to provoke Kijima into harming his wife so he could be rid of her without dirtying his own hands; (3) old file omitted that Yashiro sedated Manda at a staff drinking party specifically to destroy his alibi and shift suspicion onto him once Kijima's bar alibi checked out; (4) old file omitted the two red-herring suspects (presenter Inuyama Ninosuke, director Kujirai Mamoru) who are shown to despise Manda but are cleared of a plausible motive to kill his wife; (5) old file's single clue (script mirrors Yashiro's own history) is kept but sharpened and supplemented with the two clues that actually break the case in the transcript: a cast-credit / maiden-name match proving Towako was the miscast lead actress in Yashiro's ruined debut drama seven years ago, and Yashiro's unconscious habit of touching a band-aid on the back of her neck (concealing a scratch wound, later DNA-matched to skin found under the victim's fingernails) every time a step of her frame-up succeeded.
